articles.title: How to Specify Password Reset Email Content Before Sending Marketplace Reports
articles.excerpt: Combining account recovery with report delivery saves a message but couples an expiring security action to an unrelated attachment; keep the two jobs separate. TL;DR: a password reset email needs a se…
articles.body: Combining account recovery with report delivery saves a message but couples an expiring security action to an unrelated attachment; keep the two jobs separate. TL;DR: a password reset email needs a secure, unique, time-bound reset link, an explicit expiration time, clear instructions, and a support contact. Never include a current password. For a marketplace sending a generated report as an email attachment, the first delivery gate should establish which message is being sent before any transport gets involved. Consider a design review: a seller requests a password reset while a generated settlement report is ready for delivery. Both messages have the same destination, and a shared worker makes combining their payloads tempting.

articles.title: Mastering CSS scroll‑state() in React & Tailwind
articles.excerpt: What Is scroll‑state() and Why It Matters CSS scroll‑state() is a media query‑like feature that lets you apply styles based on the current scrolling activity of an element or the viewport. Unlike the…
articles.body: What Is scroll‑state() and Why It Matters CSS scroll‑state() is a media query‑like feature that lets you apply styles based on the current scrolling activity of an element or the viewport. Unlike the traditional :hover or :focus pseudo‑classes, scroll‑state() can detect whether the user is actively scrolling, has stopped, or has scrolled to the top or bottom. This opens up new UI possibilities such as: Showing a “Back to top” button only after the user has scrolled past a threshold. Changing a header’s background color when the page is being scrolled. Triggering lazy‑load animations when the user stops scrolling. Because the feature is purely CSS, it keeps JavaScript logic minimal and can be leveraged directly in React components.

articles.title: Avatar Thumbnail Processing Explained — Node.js Sharp, Fixed Sizes, Private Storage
articles.excerpt: Short answer: save the untouched avatar under a new versioned key, generate square 32, 64, 128, and 256 pixel variants with Sharp, keep every object private, and store those keys in the user record. P…
articles.body: Short answer: save the untouched avatar under a new versioned key, generate square 32, 64, 128, and 256 pixel variants with Sharp, keep every object private, and store those keys in the user record. Presign a variant for short-lived delivery; stream it through the application when access must be checked on every request. That policy favors predictable access control over a clever image service. It also avoids arbitrary resize work on the read path. For a B2B SaaS product, the original is the recovery source, the fixed variants cover normal UI slots, and the database is the authority that says which asset set is current.

articles.excerpt: The Aladdin sequel The Return of Jafar is often derided as a bad, cheap sequel which started Disney's direct-to-video sequel trend, but I love it
articles.body: Ever since former Disney CEO Bob Chapek released his autobiography last September, a rather unexpected Disney movie has been a topic for discussion: the direct-to-VHS sequel to Aladdin titled The Return of Jafar . Released in 1994, The Return of Jafar was the first in a long line of direct-to-VHS (and later direct-to-DVD) sequels to theatrical Disney films. Besides Aladdin , Disney made sequels to The Lion King , The Little Mermaid , Pocahontas , Mulan , and several other then-modern Disney animated features, as well as some much older classics like Cinderella and Bambi . These movies used cheaper animation produced by Disney’s TV division and were developed in far less time than Disney spends developing animated feature films .

Instead, Venus alternates between morning and evening appearances. All the while, its shifting moon-like phases and ever-changing proximity to Earth causes its brightness to wax and wane. articles.body: On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. The Mars rover Curiosity was the biggest and most powerful rover anyone had ever sent to the Red Planet. The 2-ton science laboratory is about the size of a small SUV. The mission's goal was to search for habitable environments on Mars , or evidence that the planet could have been habitable in the past. It launched on an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. About nine months later, Curiosity made a challenging landing on Mars. It successfully used a new landing technology called a sky crane to gently lower it to the surface. NASA's Curiosity rover lifts off atop a United Launch Alliance Atlas V rocket on Nov. 26, 2011 from Florida's Cape Canaveral Air Force Station.
